title: How a Neural Network Learns Part 1

scenes.text: We keep saying that AI learns. [1] But what does learning actually mean, inside a neural network? [2] Let's start a three part series, beginning with neurons, weights and biases.

Everything starts with a tiny unit called a neuron. [1] An artificial neuron is really just a small calculator. [2] It takes in some numbers, [3] multiplies each one by an importance value, [4] adds them all up, and passes on a result.

data.definition: A tiny calculator that weighs its inputs, adds them up and passes on a result.

scenes.text: Let's make it real. Should you carry an umbrella today? [1] The inputs are clues, like clouds, the weather forecast, and a humid feeling. [2] Each clue gets a weight, and the forecast matters most, so it gets the biggest weight. [3] The neuron adds up each clue times its weight, and if the total is high enough, it says, yes, take the umbrella.

Now the key words. [1] A weight is how important an input is. [2] A bias is an extra nudge, which sets how easily the neuron says yes. [3] An activation decides whether, and how strongly, the neuron fires. [4] And parameters are all the weights and biases together, the numbers the network learns.

data.heading: The key words
terms: Fire or not, and how much

scenes.text: One neuron is simple, but connect thousands of them in layers, [1] and you get a neural network. [2] The first layers pick up simple patterns, like edges. [3] Middle layers combine them into shapes. [4] And the last layer gives the answer.

So what does learning actually mean? [1] Before training, all the weights are random, so the network's answers are random guesses. [2] After training, the weights have been tuned, so the right inputs lead to the right answers. Learning simply means finding good weights.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think artificial neurons work just like brain cells. [2] They're only loosely inspired by the brain. An artificial neuron is simple maths, multiply, add and decide, while real brain cells are far more complex.

data.myth: Artificial neurons work just like brain cells.
data.fact: They're loosely inspired by the brain. An artificial neuron is simple maths: multiply, add, decide.
data.tip: Inspired by, not a copy of

scenes.text: Quick quiz! In a neural network, what does learning actually change? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] The weights and biases! Learning means finding good values for them.

Let's recap. [1] A neuron weighs its inputs, adds them up, and decides. [2] Weights say how important each input is. [3] Layers turn simple patterns into complex ones. [4] And learning means finding good weights. [5] Next, a real world breakdown, how Google Lens recognises anything you point your camera at. Follow AI Maastaaru!
